articles.title: Newscast - Russell Brand Guilty Of Rape - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three of sexual assault
articles.body: Today, comedian and actor Russell Brand has been found guilty of rape and three sexual offences and remanded in custody ahead of his sentencing next week. Adam is joined by Anoushka Mutanda-Dougherty, presenter of Fame Under Fire, who has attended every day of 51-year-old Brand’s trial. They discuss the counts the jury found Brand guilty on, how the trial unfolded and further rape allegations made by two women which can now be reported. Also, following a successful result for the democrats in the US midterm elections, how could Trump’s electoral defeat play out in the rest of the world? Adam is joined by our International Editor, Jeremy Bowen, to assess what it might mean for US involvement in the Middle East, the war between Russia and Ukraine, and Trump’s plans for Cuba. articles.title: Bengaluru woman, 70, murdered over family property dispute: How nephew plotted killing
articles.summary: Bengaluru police arrest two relatives for alleged murder of 70-year-old Venkatlakshmamma in a family property dispute on Mysuru Road, Oct 23.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A property dispute within the family turned deadly, with two distant relatives accused of murdering a 70-year-old woman who had been living alone at Hosa Guddadahalli on Mysuru Road.The accused allegedly attacked Venkatlakshmamma on the head and neck with an iron rod following an argument over her properties and fled the scene on October 23.Byatarayanapura police have arrested Kantharaju, 42, a resident of Nakkalubande in Jayanagar and nephew of the deceased’s elder brother, and Manjappa, 37, a resident of Doddabidarakallu in north Bengaluru, who is related to the victim’s foster sister.Kantharaju works as a labourer, while Manjappa is an auto driver and labourer.Venkatlakshmamma had lost her husband during the Covid-19 pandemic, while her only daughter had passed away a couple of years ago.With no immediate family members living with her, she had been staying alone in her house.She owned several properties, including one in Rajarajeshwarinagar. However, the properties were embroiled in a legal dispute with her siblings, which was pending before a court.With the help of technical assistance, police got some clues about the killers. Since some jewellery remained on the victim’s body while a few items were missing, police suspected that the murder was not necessarily motivated by robbery and that someone known to her could be involved.Probe revealed that the killers had spoken to Venkatlakshmamma about the property a few times. They visited her house on October 23.They argued with her over the same issue and killed her between 1pm and 4pm that day by attacking her with an iron rod before fleeing.The murder came to light the following day when neighbours checked on her as she had not stepped out of the house for almost 24 hours.One of her tenants had filed a complaint with police. Kantharaju confessed to police that by eliminating Venkatlakshmamma, the property would go to her brother, who is his uncle. articles.title: Roads choke, cabs burn hole in pockets: Markets across Delhi teem with Diwali shoppers
articles.summary: Diwali rush snarls Delhi traffic on major roads and markets, with travel times up to 2 hours and cab fares surging amid high demand and curbs.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Festive shopping and holiday travel brought traffic to a crawl across several parts of Delhi Thursday, with congestion reported on key arterial roads and around major markets, while commuters also grappled with a sharp surge in cab fares.Dhaula Kuan witnessed heavy traffic around 3pm, an unusually busy period for the stretch.Commuters travelling between Delhi and Noida reported journey times stretching close to two hours. Slow-moving traffic was also reported on Vikas Marg, Sardar Patel Marg, Ring Road and Outer Ring Road.The festive rush was particularly visible around popular shopping destinations, including Chandni Chowk, South Extension and Lajpat Nagar, where roads remained clogged as shoppers headed out for last-minute Diwali purchases.Barapullah Flyover emerged as another major bottleneck, with commuters reporting travel times of up to 55 minutes.The congestion drew criticism on social media, with several users complaining about delays and questioning traffic management at key junctions.“The Delhi traffic is as BAD as its air #AQI. Thirty minutes of waiting time at signals,” one commuter posted.Another wrote, “Diwali! Expected traffic madness, yet not a policeman to be seen anyplace near Khan Market or adjoining roads!”A third post highlighted the larger cost of the gridlock, saying, “So many jams in one frame. Seriously, Delhi needs professional traffic management personnel. Colossal waste of fuel and time - national wastage. Hope someone is listening.”Along with long queues on the roads, commuters were also hit by higher cab fares. Several users reported paying substantially more than usual for daily journeys amid increased demand during the festive season.Ishika, who usually pays Rs 450 for her trip to Noida, said she had to shell out Rs 700 Thursday. A cab driver attributed the surge to the Diwali rush as well as restrictions on non-BS-VI vehicles entering Delhi.Brajesh, another commuter, said, “It’s costing me Rs 1,000 every day just to commute. Pathetic.”The steep fares were also being flagged online. One commuter shared that a roughly 25 km journey from Noida Sector 15 to Shalimar Garden in Ghaziabad was attracting a fare estimate of Rs 1,600 to Rs 2,500, calling it an “outrageous loot”.Another commuter, who travelled to work by cab the previous day, described a combination of smog, endless traffic jams and soaring fares.The driver had to take a longer route via Faridabad to reach Gurgaon from Noida, the commuter said, adding that cab rides were costing almost double compared with travelling in a private vehicle.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Clear is expanding its e-gates to speed up airport security. Here’s how it works.
articles.summary: Clear is expanding its e-gates to even more airports. Here's what to know.
articles.body:
Clear's biometric identity-verification service, Clear+, helps travelers breeze through airport security — and the experience is becoming even faster. On Nov. 4, Clear said it expects to expand its e-gate program to the majority of airports that offer Clear+ by the end of the year.

Clear+ is available at 63 airports across the United States, with Tampa International as its most recent adopter. It lets travelers bypass the traditional ID check line using facial scans. Before the arrival of e-gates, travelers would go to a Clear kiosk at the airport for verification, then be met by a Clear agent who'd escort them to a TSA officer to complete the identity verification process.

The service is particularly helpful for people who are already stressed by security lines at the airport — or those attempting to test out the "airport theory" and arrive mere minutes before boarding. (Our tip? Don't do it.)

In August 2025, Clear introduced its e-gate service. With the Clear e-gate, you scan your boarding pass, then walk up to an automated gate that scans your face, allowing TSA to verify you electronically before you proceed to security screening.

It's faster and doesn't require you to be passed from one agent to the next.

What's the difference between Clear+ and TSA PreCheck?

Clear+ and TSA PreCheck are separate programs, but you can use them in tandem.

A Clear+ membership allows you to verify your identity in a dedicated lane before proceeding to security, while TSA PreCheck gives you access to an expedited security line. (And typically, it allows you to keep your laptop in your carry-on and a light jacket and belt on as well.)

Clear+ still lets you move ahead of people in the regular ID check line, even without PreCheck, meaning you'll likely save time throughout the security process — though it's not a guarantee, as Clear+ lines can also have waits.

If you have Clear+ but not PreCheck, you'll have to undergo standard passenger screening, but you might get there faster.

A Clear+ membership costs $219 per year, while TSA PreCheck costs $85 (or less) for five years ; prices can vary by enrollment provider. You can also enroll in TSA PreCheck on the Clear website and complete your application at a participating Clear location, without scheduling an appointment.

Some premium travel credit cards offer reimbursement for Clear+ and/or TSA PreCheck and Global Entry, so if you're considering a membership, check the cards in your wallet to see if you already have unused statement credits that can help make your airport security experience easier and faster.

Earning status with certain airlines can also give you a discount on Clear+ .

articles.title: Superesportivo da BYD chega a 503 km/h e bate recorde mundial de velocidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelo elétrico Yangwang U9 Xtreme superou sua própria marca e conquistou dois recordes reconhecidos pelo Guinness. Teste foi realizado em uma estrada de Abu Dhabi, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos.
articles.summary: Modelo elétrico Yangwang U9 Xtreme superou sua própria marca e conquistou dois recordes reconhecidos pelo Guinness. Teste foi realizado em uma estrada de Abu Dhabi.
articles.body:
O Yangwang U9 Xtreme, superesportivo elétrico da marca de ultraluxo da montadora chinesa BYD , atingiu 503,17 km/h e estabeleceu um novo recorde mundial de velocidade para carros de produção, segundo comunicado divulgado pela fabricante nesta sexta-feira (6).

A marca foi alcançada em 1º de novembro, durante um teste realizado em uma estrada de Abu Dhabi, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos. O veículo superou seu próprio recorde anterior, de 496,22 km/h, registrado em setembro de 2025, na Alemanha.

Segundo a BYD , o resultado garantiu ao modelo dois títulos do Guinness:

Maior velocidade alcançada por um carro de produção em uma única direção;

Maior velocidade registrada por um carro elétrico de produção nas mesmas condições.

A marca também foi reconhecida pela Federação Internacional de Automobilismo (FIA).

O carro foi conduzido pelo piloto alemão Marc Basseng, que também estava ao volante quando o veículo estabeleceu seu recorde anterior.

Para realizar o teste, as autoridades locais autorizaram o fechamento de um trecho de 10 quilômetros de estrada. A maior reta disponível tinha sete quilômetros de extensão.

Os primeiros testes ocorreram em 31 de outubro, quando o carro chegou a 490 km/h. Após ajustes na suspensão, nos pneus e na aerodinâmica, a equipe realizou mais duas tentativas em 1º de novembro. Na última delas, o superesportivo atingiu os 503,17 km/h.

Como é o carro que ultrapassou os 500 km/h?

O Yangwang U9 Xtreme é uma versão mais potente do U9 convencional, superesportivo elétrico da BYD conhecido por acelerar mais rápido que uma Ferrari e até saltar sobre buracos.

A versão que bateu o recorde tem quatro motores elétricos, um em cada roda, que entregam uma potência combinada de aproximadamente 3.019 cavalos.

O modelo também conta com uma bateria de alta potência, pneus desenvolvidos para suportar velocidades extremas e uma suspensão inteligente, capaz de realizar ajustes automáticos para manter a estabilidade.

Já o U9 convencional tem quatro motores que, juntos, entregam cerca de 1.300 cavalos de potência. O veículo acelera de 0 a 100 km/h em apenas 2,3 segundos, superando a Ferrari SF90 Stradale, que leva 2,5 segundos para atingir a mesma velocidade.

Outra característica do superesportivo chinês é a capacidade de saltar sobre buracos e até "dançar" ao som de música.

Isso é possível graças a um sistema de suspensão hidráulica que permite elevar rapidamente o veículo. Segundo a BYD, o carro consegue realizar um salto em apenas meio segundo.

Em uma demonstração divulgada pela fabricante, o U9 chegou a 120 km/h e percorreu cerca de seis metros no ar ao saltar sobre um obstáculo.

O sistema também permite que o carro realize movimentos sincronizados com música e luzes, criando a impressão de que está dançando.

O U9 convencional ainda não é vendido no Brasil. Na China, seu preço parte de 1,68 milhão de yuans (cerca de R$ 1,38 milhão).

Já o Yangwang U9 Xtreme, responsável pelo novo recorde, terá produção limitada a apenas 30 unidades em todo o mundo.

articles.title: VÍDEO: australiana salva filhote de coala de ataque de cobra | G1
articles.standfirst: As imagens não mostram o resgate em si, mas terminam com um final feliz após registrarem a mamãe coala desesperada ao ver uma cobra enrolada em seu filhote.
articles.summary: As imagens não mostram o resgate em si, mas terminam com um final feliz após registrarem a mamãe coala desesperada ao ver uma píton enrolada em seu filhote.
articles.body:
Uma australiana registrou um momento heroico que viveu ao conseguir salvar um filhote de coala do ataque de uma cobra em Brisbane, na Austrália .

As imagens, confirmadas como reais pela agência de notícias Reuters, foram registradas na terça-feira (3). Elas não mostram o resgate em si, mas terminam com um final feliz.

No começo do vídeo, a mulher corre para perto da cena, por causa dos pedidos desesperados de ajuda da mamãe coala, e encontra o filhote com a cobra enrolada em corpo dele.

Filhote de coala com píton enrolada nele — Foto: REUTERS

Depois, já aparece colocando mãe e filho em segurança em uma árvore, antes de mostrar a cobra enrolada em seu braço.

Os coalas são considerados espécie em perigo de extinção em algumas partes da Austrália, ameaçados pela perda de habitat e por doenças.

articles.title: Águas de Manaus fortalece estrutura para manter abastecimento durante estiagem  | G1
articles.standfirst: Concessionária investe em soluções permanentes e amplia a capacidade de resposta a cenários de redução do nível do rio.
articles.summary: Concessionária investe em soluções permanentes e amplia a capacidade de resposta a cenários de redução do nível do rio.
articles.body:
Ponta das Lajes Operação Estiagem 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Após três anos de investimentos e adaptações no sistema de captação de água, Manaus está mais preparada para enfrentar períodos de estiagem severa. Desde 2023, a Águas de Manaus destinou mais de R$ 25 milhões na modernização da estrutura de captação de água na cidade, com foco na prevenção de impactos de eventos climáticos extremos, garantindo que as mais de 2,2 milhões de pessoas que vivem na capital sigam com acesso à água tratada, mesmo em cenários de estiagens intensas.

Entre as ações realizadas neste ano, está uma operação preventiva na Estação de Tratamento de Água Ponta das Lajes, responsável pelo abastecimento da Zona Leste de Manaus. Em agosto, duas novas bombas anfíbias foram instaladas na unidade para reforçar a capacidade de captação do Rio Negro durante o período de seca.

Os equipamentos recebem esse nome porque podem operar submersos e também fora da água, além de conseguirem captar água do rio em níveis mais profundos. Cada bomba tem capacidade de vazão de até 550 litros por segundo e pode operar em profundidades de até 26 metros, ampliando a flexibilidade operacional do sistema.

“Em outras palavras, elas dão maior segurança operacional para o nosso sistema, principalmente porque conseguem se adaptar a situações mais extremas, como o período de estiagem. Com esses equipamentos, ampliamos nossa capacidade de captação e estamos mais preparados para cenários de redução das cotas do Rio Negro, de forma que não há preocupação com cenário de racionamento” , explica a gerente de Operações da concessionária, Jéssica Candeia.

A concessionária acompanha diariamente as cotas do Rio Negro e desenvolve estratégias operacionais para garantir a segurança do abastecimento em Manaus. O planejamento envolve a aquisição de novos equipamentos, adaptações nas estruturas existentes e a aplicação de tecnologias que, aliadas à mão de obra especializada, permitem respostas mais rápidas e eficientes diante das mudanças no cenário climático.

O trabalho realizado em 2026 dá continuidade às ações adotadas pela Águas de Manaus durante as estiagens históricas de 2023 e 2024. Na ocasião, todas as captações de água do Rio Negro foram adaptadas, com a instalação de três bombas anfíbias, sendo uma na ETA Mauazinho e duas no Complexo da Ponta do Ismael, onde funcionam duas estações de tratamento que atendem mais de 70% da população de Manaus.

Além disso, a estrutura passou por adaptações, com o rebaixamento de 13 das 16 bombas verticais que já ficam no Rio Negro, em uma operação complexa, que envolveu mergulhadores e equipamentos específicos para atuar nestas estruturas (algumas delas, datadas da década de 1960). A partir desse trabalho, foi possível captar água de pontos mais profundos do Rio Negro, o que garantiu que as bombas continuassem funcionando de forma plena e que estiagem histórica não impactasse o abastecimento na cidade.

A partir da experiência acumulada nesses períodos, a concessionária vem realizando investimentos para tornar o sistema de captação e distribuição mais resiliente diante de diferentes cenários hidrológicos.

“As bombas anfíbias instaladas na Ponta do Ismael, na operação de 2024, foram incorporadas ao sistema de abastecimento de água da capital de forma permanente, podendo, inclusive, ser transportadas para outras unidades da capital em situações emergenciais. O mesmo vai ocorrer com essa estrutura que adquirimos para a Ponta das Lajes, com um reforço que garante segurança operacional e prevenção para eventos extremos” , aponta o diretor executivo da concessionária, Renee Chaveiro.

Para o diretor-presidente da Águas de Manaus, Pedro Augusto Freitas, a antecipação é fundamental para garantir a continuidade do serviço diante dos desafios impostos pelas mudanças climáticas.

“Nos preparamos com antecedência para enfrentar um cenário desafiador. Mesmo diante das projeções de estiagem histórica pela terceira vez em quatro anos, estamos fortalecendo nossas estruturas e nossa capacidade operacional para garantir a continuidade e a regularidade do fornecimento de água tratada para a população de Manaus. Nosso compromisso é garantir a segurança hídrica da cidade, independentemente dos desafios impostos pelas mudanças climáticas” , destaca.

articles.title: Retorno da Avenida Noide Cerqueira será interditado em Feira de Santan | G1
articles.standfirst: Bloqueio serve para a implantação de um sistema inteligente de tráfego. Ação busca organizar o trânsito, prevenir acidentes e melhorar a circulação.
articles.summary: Bloqueio serve para a implantação de um sistema inteligente de tráfego. Ação busca organizar o trânsito, prevenir acidentes e melhorar a circulação.
articles.body:
Retorno da Avenida Noide Cerqueira será interditado até domingo em Feira de Santana — Foto: Divulgação | SMT

Um retorno da Avenida Noide Cerqueira, em Feira de Santana , segunda maior cidade da Bahia, será interditado a partir desta sexta-feira (6) para a implantação de um sistema inteligente de gerenciamento de tráfego. Segundo a Superintendência Municipal de Trânsito (SMT), o bloqueio seguirá até domingo (8).

O retorno fica nas proximidades do Espaço Brilhante Eventos, na entrada do Corredor dos Araçás.

Durante o período de interdição, a SMT orienta os motoristas a utilizarem os retornos seguintes da avenida e a ficarem atentos à sinalização instalada no local.

O equipamento permitirá que o acesso ao retorno seja aberto ou fechado remotamente, conforme o fluxo de veículos. A implantação vai ocorrer de forma gradual.

O sistema contará com câmeras de monitoramento integradas ao Centro de Controle da SMT. A partir das imagens, agentes poderão acompanhar o trânsito em tempo real e definir os momentos em que o retorno deverá ser liberado ou bloqueado.

De acordo com o superintendente de Trânsito, Ricardo Cunha, a iniciativa busca organizar o fluxo de veículos em um dos pontos de grande movimentação da avenida, prevenir acidentes e melhorar a circulação na região.

A SMT informou que a implantação faz parte de um conjunto de melhorias na malha viária do município.

articles.standfirst: Unidades de saúde terão atividades ao longo do mês, com orientações sobre câncer de próstata, consultas médicas e cuidados com a saúde masculina.
articles.summary: Novembro Azul no Alto Tietê oferece exames de PSA, vacinação e consultas gratuitas em diversas cidades da região para reforçar a prevenção do câncer de próstata.
articles.body:
Cidades do Alto Tietê têm programação para o Novembro Azul — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Mogi das Cruzes

As cidades do Alto Tietê prepararam ações de saúde durante o Novembro Azul, campanha de conscientização sobre a saúde masculina e a prevenção do câncer de próstata. A programação inclui coleta de exames de PSA, testes rápidos para infecções sexualmente transmissíveis (ISTs), vacinação, palestras e orientações sobre prevenção de doenças.

Entre os serviços disponíveis estão exames e atendimentos em unidades de saúde, além de atividades em espaços públicos. Algumas cidades também vão promover ações voltadas à saúde mental, alimentação saudável e acompanhamento médico.

A Prefeitura de Arujá realiza neste sábado (7), das 8h às 16h, uma ação especial do Novembro Azul no Centro de Especialidades Médicas (CEM), ao lado da Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) do Centro.

Durante o atendimento, os moradores poderão ter acesso aos seguintes serviços:

Teste de glicemia para verificar a taxa de açúcar no sangue.

Equipes de saúde também estarão disponíveis para orientar a população sobre prevenção de doenças e cuidados com a saúde masculina.

As unidades de saúde de Biritiba-Mirim terão atividades durante todo o mês de novembro. Segundo a prefeitura, a programação inclui palestras educativas, orientações sobre o câncer de próstata e informações sobre prevenção e diagnóstico precoce.

Também serão divulgados os serviços e exames disponíveis na rede municipal de saúde.

A prefeitura não informou as datas e os horários das atividades, mas orienta os moradores a procurarem a unidade de saúde de referência para obter informações e participar das ações.

articles.summary: Previsões do Inema são para cidades do oeste, extremo sul, sul do sudoeste e Vale do São Francisco. Enquanto isso, Salvador tem baixa chance de chuva no sábado (7) e domingo (8).
articles.body:
Há previsão de granizo na Bahia — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Pelo menos quatro regiões da Bahia poderão registrar chuva de granizo durante o fim de semana. A informação foi divulgada nesta sexta-feira (6), pelo Instituto do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Inema).

As previsões da chuva de granizo são para cidades do oeste, extremo sul, sul do sudoeste e Vale do São Francisco.

Enquanto isso, Salvador e cidades da região metropolitana têm baixas chances de chuva no sábado (7) e domingo (8). (Saiba mais ao fim da reportagem)

De acordo com o Inema, o oeste da Bahia já deve registrar chuvas nesta sexta-feira, além de possibilidade de trovoadas.

Apesar disso, a situação pode se agravar apenas no domingo, devido a chegada de um sistema frontal. As quatro regiões mencionadas vão registrar chuvas, que poderão vir acompanhadas de raios, rajadas de vento e granizo.

🌡️ Apesar da chuva, as temperaturas devem seguir altas em cidades das regiões extremo sul, oeste e Vale do São Francisco. De acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), as cidades deverão registrar as seguintes temperaturas no fim de semana:

Barreiras - máxima de 39ºC e mínima de 20ºC

Juazeiro - máxima de 38ºC e mínima de 21ºC

Vitória da Conquista - máxima de 39ºC e mínima de 16ºC

Porto Seguro - máxima de 37ºC e mínima de 20°C

Em Salvador, na Região Metropolitana e no Recôncavo, há baixas possibilidades de chuvas durante o fim de semana e o calor continua firme.

No domingo, dia de maior possibilidade de chuvas de granizo em quatro regiões do estado, a capital baiana e as cidades próximas terão apenas variação de nebulosidade, sem chuva prevista.

articles.title: 'Só percebi quando vi que estava ensanguentada', diz mulher esfaqueada no pescoço durante festa de Halloween na Grande SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Tainá Polegato Alves foi atingida após um desentendimento na fila do banheiro de um bar em Itapecerica da Serra. Vítima segue internada e relatou ter sofrido uma lesão em um ramo da artéria carótida.
articles.summary: Tainá Polegato Alves foi atingida após um desentendimento na fila do banheiro de um bar em Itapecerica da Serra. Vítima segue internada e relatou ter sofrido uma lesão em um ramo da artéria carótida.
articles.body:
Uma mulher foi atingida por uma faca no pescoço após um desentendimento na fila do banheiro de um bar durante uma festa de Halloween, em Itapecerica da Serra , na Grande São Paulo. O caso aconteceu na madrugada de domingo (1º).

Tainá Polegato Alves afirmou que inicialmente pensou que a arma utilizada no ataque fosse falsa. Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, Tainá contou que só percebeu a gravidade do ferimento quando viu que estava sangrando. A vítima segue internada.

“Eu demorei uns 10 segundos para entender porque era Halloween. Eu achei que era uma faca de mentira. Eu só me dei conta quando o sangue começou a espirrar.”

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, Tainá estava com amigos no Bar Cristal Rock quando foi ao banheiro e começou uma discussão com outra mulher, que a acusou de furar a fila.

A vítima afirma que houve apenas uma breve troca de palavras antes do ataque. Segundo ela, a mulher chegou a dizer que iria esfaqueá-la, mas a ameaça não foi levada a sério por causa da festa de Halloween.

“Ela me empurrou e falou: ‘Você pulou sim’. Eu falei que não.”

Imagens de uma câmera de segurança mostram o momento em que uma mulher se aproxima de Tainá, toca em seu braço e, após uma rápida troca de palavras, faz um movimento com um objeto em direção ao pescoço da vítima.

Em vídeo, Tainá relatou que teve dificuldades para engolir após o ferimento e que exames identificaram uma lesão em um ramo da artéria carótida. Segundo ela, havia a possibilidade de uma cirurgia devido a um sangramento interno.

“Eu estou conseguindo falar, mas estou com uma dificuldade de deglutir, para comer. [...] Se eu estou viva aqui hoje, é Deus mesmo.”

A mulher apontada como responsável pelo ataque foi identificada no boletim de ocorrência como Joyce Mara Rocumback Espírito Santo, de 43 anos.

De acordo com o registro policial, uma faca encontrada na bolsa da suspeita foi apreendida e encaminhada para perícia. A vítima e testemunhas também foram ouvidas.

O caso foi inicialmente registrado como lesão corporal leve e porte de arma branca e encaminhado ao Juizado Especial Criminal.

Durante o registro da ocorrência, a suspeita afirmou que não estava se sentindo bem e que fazia uso de medicamentos controlados. O Samu foi acionado e ela foi encaminhada a uma unidade de saúde.

Tainá afirmou que pretende buscar a responsabilização pelo ataque. “Pelo menos eu estou viva. Isso aqui foi um ataque pessoal, eu não posso deixar isso impune.”

“Como era Halloween, eu não levei em consideração. [...] Eu demorei uns 10 segundos para entender porque era Halloween. Eu achei que era uma faca de mentira. Eu só me dei conta quando o sangue começou a espirrar.”

Imagens da câmera de segurança do estabelecimento mostram uma mulher se aproximando e encostando no braço da vítima. (Assista no início da matéria. ATENÇÃO: IMAGENS FORTES)

Após uma rápida troca de palavras, ela retira um objeto e faz um movimento rápido contra a região do pescoço da vítima.

Em vídeo, a vítima afirmou que teve dificuldades para engolir depois do ferimento e que permanecia internada na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI).

Segundo o relato dela, exames indicaram uma lesão em um ramo da carótida e havia possibilidade de cirurgia devido a um sangramento interno.

🔍As artérias carótidas são os principais vasos sanguíneos do pescoço e têm a função de levar sangue rico em oxigênio e nutrientes do coração para o cérebro, além de abastecer estruturas da face e do pescoço.

Roupa de vítima ficou ensanguentada após ataque com faca. — Foto: Reprodução

Ela também afirmou que não houve uma discussão prolongada nem tempo para que pudesse se afastar antes do golpe.

“Não houve uma discussão, não houve uma ameaça para eu me afastar, nada. [...] Ela simplesmente falou e fez.”

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, uma faca encontrada na bolsa da mulher apontada como responsável pelo ferimento foi recolhida para perícia. Também foi solicitado exame de corpo de delito para a vítima.

Segundo o documento, duas testemunhas, a vítima e a agressora foram ouvidas.

Durante o registro do caso, a mulher apontada como responsável pelo golpe disse que não estava se sentindo bem e que fazia uso de medicamentos controlados. O Samu foi acionado para atendê-la e ela foi posteriormente encaminhada a uma unidade de saúde.

Vídeo mostra momento do esfaqueamento em bar de Itapecerica da Serra, na Grande SP. — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda de acordo com o boletim, uma equipe foi ao estabelecimento para tentar obter mais informações e imagens das câmeras de segurança, mas encontrou o local fechado.

O caso foi inicialmente registrado como lesão corporal leve e porte de arma branca e encaminhado ao Juizado Especial Criminal. A vítima também foi orientada sobre o prazo para manifestar formalmente interesse no prosseguimento do caso.

articles.title: Tesla vai reduzir gradualmente produção do Cybertruck no Texas | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudança deve ocorrer por volta de meados de 2027 e abrir espaço para ampliar a fabricação do Cybercab, veículo desenvolvido pela Tesla para operar como táxi-robô.
articles.summary: Mudança deve ocorrer por volta de meados de 2027 e abrir espaço para ampliar a fabricação do Cybercab, veículo desenvolvido pela Tesla para operar como táxi-robô.
articles.body:
A Tesla planeja reduzir gradualmente a produção do Cybertruck em sua fábrica no Texas por volta de meados do próximo ano, afirmou o presidente-executivo Elon Musk nesta sexta-feira (6). A medida deve abrir espaço para ampliar a fabricação do Cybercab, veículo da montadora desenvolvido para operar como táxi-robô.

Ainda não está claro se a produção do Cybertruck será transferida para outra unidade ou encerrada definitivamente. A fábrica da Tesla em Austin é a única unidade conhecida da montadora que produz o modelo.

A Tesla não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

“O Cybertruck foi uma plataforma incrível de desenvolvimento tecnológico e segue vivo no Cybercab”, afirmou Wes Morrill, engenheiro-chefe do Cybertruck, no X.

O Cybertruck, apresentado por Musk como um rival futurista das picapes de montadoras tradicionais, como a Ford, tem enfrentado dificuldades para conquistar o mercado de massa que o executivo projetava quando o modelo foi lançado, em 2023.

O veículo também foi alvo de vários recalls e problemas de controle de qualidade, e teve seus preços alterados diversas vezes.

Ao mesmo tempo, o Cybercab se tornou peça central da estratégia da Tesla para o mercado de táxis-robôs. Musk afirma que pretende transformar a montadora em uma empresa voltada à robótica e à direção autônoma, com o Cybercab como um dos principais veículos de sua rede de carros sem motorista.

articles.title: 'Bolo de sucuris' surpreende trabalhador às margens de rio em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Animais foram filmados em Caarapó. Fenômeno acontece quando vários machos se enrolam em uma fêmea durante o período reprodutivo.
articles.summary: O registro do bolo de sucuris no Rio Piratini, em Caarapó, mostra o fenômeno reprodutivo onde machos se entrelaçam a uma fêmea maior para disputar o acasalamento.
articles.body:
Uma cena diferente surpreendeu o pecuarista Natan Modesto, já acostumado a encontrar sucuris pelo Rio Piratini, em Caarapó (MS). Ao passar pelo local, ele encontrou várias cobras entrelaçadas, formando o chamado "bolo de sucuris", e registrou o fenômeno em vídeo. O vídeo foi compartilhado nas redes sociais dele nesta sexta-feira (6). Veja o vídeo acima.

Natan contou que passava pelo local quando encontrou os animais e chegou a ficar a cerca de cinco metros de distância. Apesar de já ter visto uma sucuri naquele trecho do rio, nunca tinha presenciado tantas juntas.

O registro foi especial para Natan, que disse ter ficado emocionado ao presenciar o fenômeno. " Eu já tinha visto a cobra lá antes, mas não aquele bolo", contou ao g1.

Cobras entrelaçadas em rio de MS — Foto: Natan Modesto

Em entrevista ao g1 , o biólogo Henrique Abrahão explicou que o fenômeno acontece durante o período de reprodução. As fêmeas liberam substâncias chamadas feromônios, que atraem vários machos ao mesmo tempo.

Os machos ficam enrolados ao redor da fêmea, formando o chamado "bolo de sucuris". Segundo o especialista, é a fêmea que escolhe com qual deles vai acasalar.

Henrique também explicou que as fêmeas são bem maiores que os machos, podendo chegar a quase o dobro do tamanho deles.

articles.title: Mato Grosso tem segundo início de safra mais seco em 27 anos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuvas ficaram 33% abaixo da média histórica entre setembro e outubro. Entidade alerta que lavouras já sentem os efeitos da falta de umidade, apesar do avanço do plantio.
articles.summary: Chuvas ficaram 33% abaixo da média histórica entre setembro e outubro. Entidade alerta que lavouras já sentem os efeitos da falta de umidade, apesar do avanço do plantio.
articles.body:
O cenário coloca em dúvida as projeções mais otimistas para a safra 2026/2027 — Foto: Reprodução

Mato Grosso enfrenta o segundo início de safra mais seco dos últimos 27 anos, e a falta de chuva já preocupa produtores de soja . Entre 1º de setembro e 27 de outubro, o estado registrou 186 milímetros de precipitação, volume 33% menor que a média histórica para o período, de acordo com um levantamento da EnsoAg/SmartCampo, feito com dados da NASA e divulgado pela Associação dos Produtores de Soja e Milho de Mato Grosso (Aprosoja-MT).

O cenário coloca em dúvida as projeções mais otimistas para a safra 2026/2027. Mesmo com o plantio avançando, produtores relatam lavouras afetadas pela baixa umidade do solo, principalmente em regiões do Oeste e Médio-Norte do estado.

A situação é mais preocupante na região dos Parecis. Em Campos de Júlio , por exemplo, foram registrados apenas 89 milímetros de chuva nos 30 dias analisados, quantidade 56% abaixo do esperado. Brasnorte , Comodoro e Sapezal também tiveram volumes bem inferiores à média histórica.

O levantamento aponta ainda que 22 dos 23 municípios avaliados tiveram menos chuva que o esperado. Em 66% do território mato-grossense, o volume de precipitação ficou pelo menos 25% abaixo do padrão histórico.

Além da pouca chuva, as temperaturas elevadas e a distribuição irregular das precipitações aumentam o risco de prejuízos ao desenvolvimento das plantas.

Segundo o presidente da Aprosoja-MT, Lucas Costa Beber, algumas lavouras semeadas mais cedo já chegaram à fase reprodutiva e começam a sentir os efeitos da falta de água. Ele alerta que o avanço do plantio não significa que a produção esteja garantida.

As chuvas registradas entre 28 de outubro e 1º de novembro trouxeram um pouco de alívio, mas ainda ficaram 22% abaixo da média esperada para o período. A entidade também aponta possíveis dificuldades no controle de plantas daninhas e pragas, o que pode exigir mudanças no manejo e aumentar os custos de produção.

Apesar das preocupações, ainda não é possível calcular eventuais perdas na safra. A avaliação é de que as estimativas de uma produção elevada precisam ser confirmadas conforme o desenvolvimento das lavouras nas próximas semanas.

articles.summary: Conhecido pelos muitos afilhados e pelo hábito de reunir pessoas queridas em torno da mesa, para eles, cozinhar juntos é uma forma de acolher quem chega.
articles.body:
No Receita Família casal ensina receita de panquecas — Foto: Reprodução

O prato do quadro Receita de Família desta sexta-feira (6) é presença garantida nos encontros de amigos e familiares de Edni Corrêa da Silva e Adilza Soares de França Silva, em Cuiabá . Bem-humorado, o casal é conhecido pelos muitos afilhados e pelo hábito de reunir pessoas queridas em torno da mesa.

No bairro Jardim Imperial 2, onde moram, os dois compartilham a fama de preparar uma panqueca especial, que faz sucesso nos encontros em casa . Para eles, cozinhar juntos é uma forma de acolher quem chega, sempre com muito carinho, afeto e sabor.

Em um liquidificador ou tigela, misture o leite, os ovos, a manteiga, a cebola, o sal, o fermento e a farinha de trigo aos poucos até obter uma massa líquida e homogênea. Frite as massas em uma frigideira untada até dourar levemente dos dois lados, e reserve.

Para o recheio, em uma panela, refogue o alho e a cebola, adicione o patinho moído e mexa até dourar. Acrescente os tomates picados e os temperos a gosto, deixando apurar até que o recheio esteja bem suculento.

Já no molho utilize outra panela, para dourar o alho e a cebola picada, junte os tomates, o orégano, a noz-moscada, o sal e o sachê de molho de tomate. Deixe cozinhar em fogo lento até formar um molho encorpado e aromático.

Por fim recheie cada panqueca com a carne moída, enrole-as, disponha em uma travessa, cubra com o molho caprichado e finalize com as fatias de queijo muçarela.

articles.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
articles.summary: Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state".
articles.body:
Macau has sentenced an ex-lawmaker and pro-democracy campaigner to 12 years and six months' jail in the city's first national security case.

Following a closed-door trial, Au Kam San, 69, was convicted on Friday of "subversion against the political power of the state", among other offences.

His wife Virginia Cheang condemned the ruling, calling the case a "groundless persecution designed to humiliate Au".

Macau was handed back to China in 1999, ending over 400 years of Portuguese administration. Its national security law came into effect in 2009, criminalising acts of treason, secession, and subversion against the Chinese Communist Party.

The law was revised in 2023, broadening its scope to include non-violent acts of secession, and again this year, to allow for trials to be held behind closed doors.

Prosecutors had accused Au of assisting and collaborating with "external hostile organisations" by collecting, preparing and disseminating information that was "manifestly filled with political claims of a subversive nature against the state".

These took place "over a long period of time", the prosecutors claim.

Au was arrested in July 2025 and later charged with three counts of subverting the state's power, three counts of endangering national security by establishing contact with foreign organisations, and one count of breach of confidentiality.

He was found guilty of four of the seven charges following a three-day trial which ended in September. A judge had ordered that the trial be held behind closed doors "to ensure that no prejudice is caused to the interests of national security".

Macau's authorities never publicly disclosed the details of the case. Au's family had earlier told the media Au was not allowed to seek his own legal representation and had instead been assigned a lawyer by the court.

Au's wife Cheang said she hoped authorities would grant her and her family permission to regularly write to and visit Au in prison.

"I dare not hope for more as I believe that will only lead to greater disappointment," she said in an open letter on Friday.

Au, who was formerly a primary school teacher, was elected to the Legislative Assembly in September 2001. For 20 years, he served as one of only a handful of pro-democracy lawmakers in the legislature, largely made up of pro-Beijing loyalists.

Au had co-organised annual vigils in Macau to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing.

These vigils were previously tolerated in places like Macau and Hong Kong, but have effectively been banned in both cities since China imposed a sweeping national security law on Hong Kong in 2020.

Au's jailing comes a day after Hong Kong sentenced Joshua Wong, the face of its now-quashed democracy movement, to 10 years in jail . Wong, 30, whose activism started when he was just a teen, has been in custody for the last six years.

articles.title: Singapore man Lim Kah Kheng tricked more than 12,600 people into donating over $106,000 through a fake charity scheme; he was jailed for 46 months
articles.summary: A Singapore man was sentenced to 46 months after being convicted of cheating people through a donation scam.
articles.body: A Singapore man was sentenced to 46 months after being convicted of cheating people through a donation scam. Lim Kah Kheng, 42, was convicted on 17 November 2025 on four counts of cheating under Section 420 of the Penal Code 1871. The scam involved counterfeit staff passes and fraudulent documents, which he used while presenting the activities as social entrepreneurship and charitable work.He recruited seven people and misled them into believing they were taking part in legitimate charitable activities, before deceiving members of the public. According to a joint media release by the Singapore Police Force and the Office of the Commissioner of Charities (2025), the operation affected more than 12,600 victims and collected fraudulent donations exceeding $106,000.How was Lim Kah Kheng convicted in the Singapore donation scamLim was convicted on 17 November 2025 and sentenced to 46 months’ imprisonment. The 42-year-old was convicted and sentenced to 46 months’ imprisonment for four counts of cheating under Section 420 of the Penal Code 1871. Eight other counts of cheating under Section 420 and three counts of theft in a dwelling under Section 380 of the Penal Code 1871 were also taken into consideration for sentencing.The operation also targeted residential areas. The investigation began after the Police received a report about a man asking residents for donations near Bedok North Street 3 on 24 June 2024. The Police received a report that a man was knocking on doors and asking for donations in the vicinity of Bedok North Street 3.Fake staff passes helped Lim Kah Kheng deceive 12,600 peopleInvestigations found that Lim orchestrated the scam between 28 January 2020 and 24 June 2024. He created counterfeit staff passes and fraudulent documents to support the operation. He presented the activities as social entrepreneurship and charitable work. Lim recruited seven individuals and misled them into believing they were participating in legitimate charitable activities.He then deceived members of the public into making donations under false pretences. The operation targeted residential areas, that affected more than 12,600 victims and collecting fraudulent donations exceeding $106,000.Singapore authorities issue safety advice to prevent donation scamsThe Police and the Office of the Commissioner of Charities urged the public to remain careful when approached by fund-raisers.People should ask who will receive the donations, how the money will be used, and how much will reach the intended beneficiary.Check the Charity Portal to confirm whether a fund-raiser is a registered charity in Singapore or holds a valid foreign fund-raising permit.The authorities also advised people not to share personal information, credit card details or online account details with anyone they do not know or trust.Anyone unsure about an appeal should avoid donating under pressure and can give directly through the organisation's official website.Suspected scams should be reported to the Police.How does Singapore law deal with cheating and theftUnder Section 420 of Singapore's Penal Code 1871, anyone convicted of cheating can face a fine and imprisonment for up to 10 years. Lim's case involved four cheating charges that resulted in a 46-month prison sentence. Another eight cheating charges under the same section and three theft-in-dwelling charges under Section 380 were considered during sentencing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Google founder Sergey Brin wins battle against tax that made many billionaires 'flee' California; but clock may have started ticking again; as these three tax proposals target rich
articles.summary: Sergey Brin, the Google co-founder who previously fought and helped block California’s proposed wealth-tax measures, may have won one battle against
articles.body: Sergey Brin, the Google co-founder who previously fought and helped block California’s proposed wealth-tax measures, may have won one battle against billionaire-focused taxation. However, the political landscape in Washington suggests that the wealthy Americans could soon face renewed scrutiny as Democrats regain control of Congress and revive efforts to make billionaires pay more tax. This renewed debate follows what many business leaders viewed as a significant victory over state-level wealth-tax proposals in California, where critics that high-net-worth individuals could be taxed even after leaving the state. Opponents said such measures contributed to fears of an exodus of wealthy residents and entrepreneurs. While those proposals never become law, tax experts say the focus has now shifted to federal-level initiatives aimed at the richest Americans, as reported by CNBC.Sergey Brin’s campaign against Prop 40Prop 40 proposed a one-time 5% tax on the assets of roughly 200 California billionaires. Its backers, led by the state’s powerful healthcare workers’ union, wanted the money mostly for healthcare, to offset cuts to Medi-Cal for low-income residents. Brin was the biggest single donor against it. He contributed $102 million to fight Prop 40. Billionaire opponents and business interests put $316.7 million into the campaign to stop it, and opponents also put two countermeasures on the ballot, Props 41 and 42, designed to cancel the tax. Prop 42 would have banned wealth taxes in the state altogether. Brin also stood as an example of the flight risk that opponents invoked. They argued that billionaires would follow the paths of Elon Musk to Austin and Brin to Miami Beach, changing their residency to avoid the tax. Brin was one of the four richest Californians, with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Google co-founder Larry Page and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.According to a Los Angeles Times estimate, they would have owed 40% of the tax revenue. Gov. Gavin Newsom also came out against the measure, and Prop 40 exposed divisions among Democrats. Opponents outspent its supporters heavily, and early returns showed the measure losing. With about half the projected votes counted, 55.6% of voters had rejected it. At the time of reporting, the race had not been formally called.Democrats signal fresh push on billionaire taxationFollowing sweeping Democratic victories in the midterm elections, Ron Wyden, who is expected to retake control of the Senate Finance Committee, indicated that taxing the wealthy will remain a priority. “On taxes, the committee will redouble its efforts to ensure billionaires pay their fair share and hold tax cheats accountable,” Wyden said, according to CNBC.Tax attorneys told CNBC that most of the proposals are unlikely to become law in the near term because President Donald Trump could veto them. However, they say the bills offer a clear indication of the policies Democrats may pursue if they regain the White House and unified control of Congress in the future.Proposal 1: Ending the carried-interest tax breakOne proposal gaining renewed attention is the Ending the Carried Interest Loophole Act, introduced by Ron Wyden and Angus King. Under current rules, private equity and hedge fund managers can have portions of their earnings taxed at lower capital gains rates if investments are held for a certain period. The proposed legislation would instead tax those profits as ordinary income and accelerate when taxes are paid.The so-called carried-interest loophole has been criticised by lawmakers from both parties for years. Even President Trump has previously argued the provision gives wealthy fund managers an unfair advantage over ordinary workers. Tax experts told CNBC that carried interest reforms could eventually become part of a broader tax package designed to raise revenue, particularly as lawmakers confront concerns about the long-term funding of Social Security.Proposal 2: Annual taxes on massive trustsA second proposal, the Fair Trusts for Fiscal Responsibility Act, targets ultra-wealthy families that use large trusts as estate-planning tools. The bill, introduced by Patty Murray, would impose annual taxes on trust assets exceeding $50 million, with rates rising to 3% for assets above $1 billion.As per a tax professional quoted by CNBC, this measure could help in fundamentally reshaping the estate planning for some of America’s wealthiest individuals. However, experts question the practicality of implementing such a system, they believe the proposal excludes the growing political interests in taxing wealth held within trusts rather than waiting until asses are transferred.Proposal 3: Cracking down on the 'buy, borrow, die' strategyPerhaps the most closely watched proposal is the Redistribution Of Billions by Instituting New High-income Obligations on Overlooked Debt (ROBINHOOD) Act of 2026. The bill seeks to address the so-called "buy, borrow, die" strategy often associated with billionaires such as Larry Ellison and Elon Musk. Under the strategy, wealthy individuals borrow against appreciating stock holdings instead of selling shares and triggering capital gains taxes.The Senate bill, introduced by Ruben Gallego, would require certain ultra-wealthy borrowers to pay taxes on gains linked to assets used as collateral for loans. A related House proposal would levy a 20% tax on selected asset-backed loans for higher-income borrowers. As per the CNCB report some wealth-planning experts feel that these proposals may have a greater chance of advancing than broader wealth-tax plans because they target specific tax strategies rather than attempting to tax unrealised gains directly.You use AI every day. articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed did not have to become less Muslim to win
articles.summary: His historic victory in Michigan shows that Muslim Americans need not abandon their identity to succeed in politics.
articles.body:
Messages popped up on my WhatsApp account from New York, Gaza, Pakistan and Australia. Friends and colleagues were following Michigan’s Senate race, talking excitedly about Abdul El-Sayed. As the results from Wayne County sealed his victory on Tuesday, I felt something I had rarely felt before in American politics: not a muted relief that someone had lost but genuine joy and hope that someone had won.

El-Sayed, a physician and former Detroit health director, defeated Republican Mike Rogers . He will be the first Muslim ever elected to the United States Senate. As a Muslim American from Michigan, this hit home.

Like many in Michigan’s Muslim community, I knew of Abdul long before he became a fixture in national headlines, from his 2018 gubernatorial campaign to his Friday sermons in local mosques. As Ramadan began this year, I attended one of his town halls for Muslim constituents. Before a few dozen community members and leaders, Abdul pledged to fight for all Michiganders. His sincerity and commitment to that pledge remained evident even as the pressures of the campaign intensified. I have seen him attend funerals for community members near my home and watched him go from person to person, greeting people with kindness. Even in the final days of an exhausting campaign, he responded personally to messages from the community, including mine.

We attended the same university, the University of Michigan, where he once helped lead the Muslim Students’ Association. I later served as a college student body president there. Just days before the election, Muslim alumni (including me) invited him to a football tailgate party with students, parents and graduates. His former teachers and students have spoken to me with pride about the person they knew.

Muslim Americans are often asked to celebrate any politician who occasionally says “salaam” or appears in a mosque before Election Day. Abdul was not an outsider to our community coming to court us. He belonged to it.

During the campaign, I welcomed hundreds of local Muslim community members, out-of-state political candidates canvassing for him and members of his staff into my home. People heard from those closest to him what this race could mean for Muslim Americans. The enthusiasm felt different from the familiar, dispiriting bargain of voting mainly to stop someone worse.

Two years ago, I wrote about why I would vote against genocide in the 2024 presidential election. That decision was shaped by my work with Palestinian healthcare workers, by witnessing the realities in Palestine firsthand and by outrage at the Biden-Harris administration’s complicity in the genocide in Gaza. Neither I nor many of Michigan’s Muslims have forgotten. But this time, the ballot offered something other than just a protest vote: a candidate who had opposed Israel’s genocide against Palestinians from the outset while also caring about the range of issues affecting Michiganders.

His willingness to speak truth to power attracted immense hostility from Washington’s elites. President Donald Trump repeatedly mocked Abdul’s name , treating “Muhammad” – his middle name, meaning “the praised one” – as an insult. Political opponents and even some voters insinuated that his faith alone made him suspect, recycling unsubstantiated allegations tying him to groups and movements he did not belong to.

Abdul responded with dignity and directness. When critics made his name the issue, he spoke about groceries, housing, healthcare and affordability. When challenged over his opposition to genocide, he questioned the premise that wanting children to live free of bombs was somehow hateful. He did not accept the proposition that a Muslim must disown his community or Palestine to qualify for public office.

And most importantly, he fought back. Many Muslim voters I spoke to felt they had found someone willing to fight for them, to challenge the presumptions and racism of journalists, pundits and media outlets rather than accept their unjust framing.

His victory speech began with the words his opponents had tried to weaponise: “My name is Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed.” He recalled having said “inshallah” – “God willing” – whenever he was asked about winning. Now, he said, it was time for “alhamdulillah”, or “Praise be to God.”

That moment was electric, not because Arabic phrases alone are a sign of solidarity – even former President Joe Biden said “inshallah” in a debate before proceeding to commit genocide against Palestinians and aid the bombing of mosques and burning of Qurans – but because his Muslim identity had survived a countrywide effort by special interest groups and racists to make it disqualifying. His faith, Islam, is a value system he actively chooses every day, a commitment he strives to live out in public life. His being Muslim mattered to me more than his Arab ethnicity or ancestral origins, a simple happenstance of birth.

There was money behind the attempt to stop him too. The American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s (AIPAC’s) affiliated super PAC spent roughly $30m in Michigan’s Democratic primary, an extraordinary investment to defeat someone who openly opposed US support for Israel’s genocide and apartheid. In his victory speech, Abdul thanked AIPAC for the chance to beat it twice. One loss will not dissolve the lobbying group’s power. But Michigan demonstrated that AIPAC spending need not amount to a veto over who can win.

After Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s victory in New York , sceptics suggested that a Muslim candidate outspoken about Palestine could only win in a liberal metropolis, not a state that Trump carried in 2024. El-Sayed travelled from small towns and villages to industrial cities and suburbs, visiting churches and mosques, and he won statewide.

Michigan has long been a centre of Muslim American life, from Dearborn’s famous Arab restaurants and coffee houses to Hamtramck, the first Muslim-majority city in the US. Generations have built mosques, schools, businesses and institutions while enduring suspicion and discrimination. There is irony in Michigan electing a Muslim alumnus of the University of Michigan, which has faced legal challenges over its treatment of antigenocide protesters. Some of the voices that were treated as dangerous on campus found a home at the ballot box for the first time.

Other Muslims across the country made history too. My mentor, friend and colleague Adam Hamawy, with whom I served on a medical mission in Palestine documenting harm to people’s health, won his congressional race in New Jersey and travelled to Michigan to support Abdul. Darializa Avila Chevalier, Aber Kawas, Nabeela Syed and so many others won seats in Congress and state legislatures across the country, refusing to accept that their silence on human rights abuses is the price of participation.

Yet our celebration does not mean we have suspended all judgement. Some Muslims I spoke with vehemently opposed Abdul’s decision to campaign alongside former Vice President Kamala Harris and former President Barack Obama . Their administrations’ policies, from facilitating the genocide in Gaza to conducting drone strikes against civilians in multiple Muslim-majority countries, remain at the forefront of people’s minds. I understood their anger and shared their apprehensions about normalising the killers of children. Yet many of us still voted for Abdul because we believed in his sincerity and because he had repeatedly made clear that he did not agree with every policy of those backing his campaign. I am under no illusion that one senator alone will end the systems and structures of exploitation that fund war machines abroad and fail their own communities at home. Muslim representation risks becoming hollow if mistaken for the only tool for liberation.

And that is precisely why the substance of his campaign matters. Abdul connected the fight against endless war to the fight for healthcare, clean water and a liveable wage. He spoke of a mother trying to keep her children on lifesaving medication and a worker fighting for a union. He insisted that the money spent destroying someone else’s children has a cost for children in the US too. His politics asked whether Americans could both recognise their own self-interest and show humanity towards others.

His election does not make US government policies any more just overnight. It does not bring back a single Palestinian child. It does not absolve the Democrats, Washington or any of us of complicity. And it certainly does not entitle Abdul to six years in the Senate without scrutiny.

But it destroys one convenient lie: that Muslim Americans must choose between being unapologetically Muslim and belonging fully to American public life.

For years, we were told to lower our voices, soften our names and reconsider what we advocate for if we wanted to succeed. On Tuesday, Michigan delivered its verdict. The man they tried to make unelectable will now sit in the US Senate. Alhamdulillah, he does not need to become less Muslim to serve his state – and the rest of us do not need to police who we are to demand a better future for ourselves and the generations to come.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: In 1583, a ship returning from Spain wrecked off Wales; 443 years later, scientists used CT scans to crack the four-letter code of its brass combination lock without damaging the centuries-old mechanism
articles.summary: A ship returning from Spain was caught in a violent storm and wrecked off the coast of Wales in 1583.
articles.body: A ship returning from Spain was caught in a violent storm and wrecked off the coast of Wales in 1583. Among the objects recovered from the wreck was a brass combination lock that remained closed for more than four centuries. Researchers have now solved its four-letter code without forcing it open, using advanced CT scanning technology to examine the delicate mechanism.Cardiff University announced the discovery on November 4, 2026, following research conducted with Amgueddfa Cymru, also known as Museum Wales. The researchers successfully identified the combination as ANCE and opened the lock without damaging it. The discovery has helped solve a centuries-old puzzle, although researchers are still uncertain about what the lock originally protected and why its owner chose those four letters.A ship lost off the Welsh coastThe ship, named Ann Francis, was returning from Spain when it encountered a severe storm on December 28, 1583. Blown off course, it eventually wrecked on Margam Beach, near Port Talbot in south Wales. Much of its cargo remained buried beneath the sand for centuries. Metal detectorist Peter Hughes discovered most of the recovered treasure over 21 years, between 1996 and 2017. Storms and dredging gradually removed layers of sand at Margam Beach, exposing coins and other objects from the sixteenth-century vessel.The brass combination lock was among the recovered items. Its rotating letter rings remained movable despite spending centuries beneath the sand, but nobody could open it. The artefact was subsequently acquired by Amgueddfa Cymru and became the subject of further investigation.CT scans revealed the hidden combinationInstead of attempting to force the lock open and risk damaging it, researchers from Amgueddfa Cymru collaborated with specialists at Cardiff University to examine its internal structure. Dr David Williams, a research associate at Cardiff University's School of Engineering, used micro-CT scanning to produce detailed three-dimensional images of the lock's internal mechanism. The technology allowed researchers to examine components that could not be seen from the outside.By studying the positions of the internal notches and their alignment with the letters on the rotating rings, the team identified the four-letter combination as ANCE. Researchers then tested the combination and successfully opened the lock, confirming that their findings were correct. The process allowed them to unlock the centuries-old object without physically dismantling or damaging its mechanism.Williams explained that the scanning facility was normally used to examine bones and other biological structures, making the investigation of a historic combination lock an unusual application of the technology.What could the lock have protected?Although researchers have discovered how to open the lock, its original purpose remains a mystery. They believe it may have secured a small chest containing valuable belongings. The lock was discovered near Spanish silver coins and two coin weights recovered from the shipwreck. This has led researchers to consider whether it might have protected valuable objects or a collection of personal belongings.However, the contents of the possible chest have not been established. Researchers believe it could have contained items such as documents or textiles that have not survived the centuries since the wreck. Alastair Willis, senior curator for numismatics and the Welsh economy at Amgueddfa Cymru, said that Elizabethan combination locks were known in Britain, but this example was particularly interesting because of its condition and its connection to a shipwreck with a recorded date.Researchers are also interested in understanding whether the letters ANCE had a personal or symbolic significance for the person who originally set the combination.Historic treasure goes on displayThe brass lock is among the Ann Francis shipwreck artefacts featured in the Tides of Treasure exhibition at the National Waterfront Museum in Swansea. The collection also includes rare gold coins from the reign of Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain and a boatswain's whistle recovered from the wreck. The treasure was acquired for Wales's national collection with support from the Welsh Government.The discovery has revealed how a centuries-old combination lock worked while preserving its original mechanism. Although the meaning of its four-letter code and the identity of the person who set it remain unknown, modern scanning technology has helped researchers unlock another part of the story of the Ann Francis, more than 400 years after the ship sank.You use AI every day. articles.title: Paul Mackenzie: Kenya doomsday cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison for Shakahola deaths
articles.summary: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".
articles.body:
A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.

Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity.

"The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law," the judge added.

The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast. The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention.

The court sentenced Mackenzie to 100 years in prison for homicide and another 100 years for offences related to starvation.

The sentences within each category will run concurrently, but the two sets will run consecutively, bringing his total prison term to 200 years.

Mackenzie also faces separate manslaughter and terrorism charges, which he denies.

Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that the scale and circumstances of the killings warranted the harshest punishment.

However, Justice Mochache declined to impose the death penalty, despite ruling that the case met the threshold for its consideration.

"Nevertheless, the court declines the invitation to impose the death penalty on any of the victims," she said, adding that capital punishment would eliminate any prospect of rehabilitation and disengagement. The death sentence has not been carried out in Kenya since 1987.

Mackenzie was tried alongside 28 accomplices, including guards who enforced his fasting orders and gravediggers who helped conceal the victims' bodies in mass graves.

They received varying prison sentences of up to 160 years.

Justice Mochache described the killings as "cold and calculated", saying the perpetrators had shown no remorse and had even declared their willingness to fast to death themselves.

Before the hearing began on Friday morning, Francis Wanje, who lost eight relatives including two grandchildren in Shakahola forest, told the BBC's Newsday programme that he was "hoping for... a sentence which will match his [Mackenzie's] deeds in the forest".

Mackenzie and the co-accused had asked for leniency from the court.

Before their conviction on 19 October, they had all pleaded not guilty and repeatedly insisted that nobody was forced to die.

Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece", Justice Mochache said as she delivered her eight-hour judgement last month.

Those who opposed Mackenzie's teachings were beaten to death.

One of his co-accused said he had told his followers that anyone who "resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows".

Burials inside the forest where the cult was based were called "weddings" and those who died "were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus" the judge said.

The judge found that the deaths arose from an organised system, including religious teachings and directives that compelled followers to follow the deadly fasting.

Post-mortem results showed the cause of deaths to be starvation for most victims, while others died from suffocation, strangulation or head injuries.

The cause of death could not be determined for some, with their bodies having decomposed, while others died soon after their rescue as they were so emaciated.

The Shakahola deaths have shone a spotlight on the lack of oversight of rogue religious activities and how they could have carried on for so long.

The gravity of the case prompted President William Ruto to set up a commission of inquiry, although this was later declared unconstitutional.

Investigations by the state-funded Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) revealed that local administration and law enforcement officials had repeatedly turned a blind eye to the cult's activities.

"We expected at that time the police would take action immediately to go and rescue the other members there, but it didn't happen," said Wanje, who reported the case to the police in March 2023.

Wanje said a relative of his in the police force and a former cult participant had managed to save his grandson at the time. The child told the police what had happened and showed them the grave of his siblings.

"It was [supposed to be] his last day.. they [would have killed] my grandson."

The cult leader had previously been arrested and later released for lack of evidence.

Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003.

Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity, drawing thousands of followers in its branches across Kenya.

The church ran a television station called Times TV which would broadcast his sermons from his church in Malindi.

His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil".

The main church shut down in 2019 and Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him.

While the conclusion of the murder cases may bring a sense of justice for the victims and their families, the convictions only account for 191 victims, while more than 400 bodies were exhumed from the forest.

articles.title: Algorithm allocates Highland 'significant increase' in asylum-seeking children
articles.summary: Highland Council says the formula fails to take into consideration housing challenges it is facing.
articles.body:
Highland Council says a Home Office algorithm has allocated it with a "significant increase" in unaccompanied asylum-seeking children to look after.

The local authority said it had received national recognition for its work with the young people, many of them fleeing war or persecution.

But it said the rise in numbers would be challenging due to a lack of housing in its area, adding that the algorithm did not take into account the local situation.

The Home Office said councils had a statutory duty to support children arriving in the UK without a parent or guardian, and it was committed to working closely with authorities to help them meet their obligations.

More stories from the Highlands and Islands

News from the Highlands and Islands on BBC Sounds

Unaccompanied asylum-seeking children (UASC) are those under the age of 18 who arrive in the UK to apply for international protection on their own, without the support of an adult.

Many of them are fleeing their homeland because of political or religious persecution, war or famine.

There are 380 UASCs being looked after in Scotland, according to Scottish government figures for 31 July 2025 .

Highland Council is currently responsible for 72.

The council said it was contacted by local authorities body Cosla in July about a revised Home Office rota allocation formula.

In a report , officials said this had presented it with "significant challenges" and five times its previous number of UASCs.

Previously, Highland Council took into its care system one child per cycle, but this has now gone up to five.

There can be a period of two weeks to a number of months between cycle, depending on how many children arrive in the UK.

Highland Council officials added: "The Home Office algorithm by itself is not an adequate tool without some understanding of local conditions.

"For example, the fact that Highland has significant housing challenges, both in terms of housing availability and cost, coupled with a lack of available workforce, means Highland is not an attractive option for asylum support providers."

The local authority has previously said its area needs an extra 24,000 houses over the next 10 years . New homes are needed to address a long-standing shortage of affordable homes.

The officials also said the Home Office had not so far placed any adult asylum seekers in the Highlands.

"This lack of adult asylum seekers in Highland has had the effect of increasing the number of UASC in 2026," they said.

Eligible UASCs, like other young people in foster, kinship or residential care can remain under local authority care up to the age of 21.

Some care leavers are eligible for support up to their 26th birthday.

Highland Council receives core funding of £143 per child, per day for under 18s. For over 18s it is £270 per week.

The Home Office said it was a priority to ensure vulnerable children received the care and support they needed.

A spokesperson said: ''Local authorities have a statutory duty to support unaccompanied asylum-seeking children and care leavers, and we are committed to working closely with them to help them meet these obligations.

"Through the National Transfer Scheme, we work with local authorities across the UK to ensure responsibility for supporting unaccompanied children is shared fairly."

articles.title: Irish media outlets evacuated after receiving threats
articles.summary: Gardaí say they are "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".
articles.body:
A number of high-profile media organisations, including Ireland's public service broadcaster RTÉ, were evacuated because of bomb threats on Friday morning.

Staff at the Irish Independent newspaper and Dublin-based radio station NewstalkFM also left their offices for a short time after receiving threats by email.

The Irish government has described the bomb warnings as "hoax threats" and said the authorities were "working to establish who is responsible".

Security threats were also sent to several media outlets across Europe on Friday, including the UK broadcaster Sky.

The threats disrupted some live programme in Ireland, while other broadcasters managed to stay on air.

Armed gardaí (Irish police) were deployed to search RTÉ's headquarters in Donnybrook, Dublin, after senior staff reported the bomb threat to them.

RTÉ presenter Sarah McInerney was broadcasting at the time.

"An email had been sent to the RTÉ newsroom at 08:33 with the subject line: 'Message to the West and it had threatened that a bomb was going to go off in the next 45 minutes," she said.

"The newsroom contacted management, who contacted the gardaí and after some discussion it was decided that even through it was probably a hoax, it was better to evacuate."

Virgin Media Ireland said it also "received a security threat email that was widely circulated to multiple European media platforms".

"We followed our well established security protocols and continue to liaise with An Garda Síochána.

"We remained on air throughout and no evacuation took place."

The Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin described situation as "worrying" adding his government's first priority was the safety of the Irish public.

"Yesterday, there appeared to be coordinated efforts to disrupt air travel," he said.

He was referring to hoax bomb threats which affected 21 flights across Europe on Thursday, including Ryanair and Aer Lingus planes.

Martin told RTÉ it was not yet known if the threats had come from individuals or if it was a "coordinated attack".

"The gardaí, the defence forces, cyber and aviation authorities are working to establish who's behind this, as are their European counterparts," Martin said.

He added: "It just illustrates how relatively simple it can be to cause disruption and to undermine the normal operation of society through unconventional activities of this kind, which are designed to cause disruption, designed to cause fear and anxiety."

Tánaiste (Deputy Prime Minister) Simon Harris said it was a "very serious and evolving situation".

"Obviously this comes on the back of a number of bomb scares yesterday and in recent days in relation to airlines as well," he told Cork 96FM.

"I think it's fair to say we don't yet know who is responsible for what's happening this morning."

He said Irish authorities and cyber experts would be "liaising as appropriate with European counterparts" to identify the culprits.

Broadcaster Sky confirmed it had received a security threat, hours after RTÉ had evacuated its building.

The broadcaster, which is owned by Comcast, said in a statement read by a presenter on its news channel that the broadcaster had "carried out a security assessment and reported the matter to the relevant authorities".

"The safety and security of our colleagues is our primary concern, and we are working closely with authorities to ensure our people and operations remain secure."

Returning to her microphone at NewstalkFM, presenter Claire Byrne told listeners the threat her station received had been judged to be fake.

"Just like many other media organisations in Ireland today we were advised to leave the building today on foot of a message that we received.

"We've been in touch with the gardaí - everybody left. We were advised that we could return to the building and that that warning was a hoax."

On the social media platform X, NewstalkFM said: "Bauer Media offices were evacuated this morning after receiving a hoax bomb threat.

"We can report that everyone is safe and we are back on air as normal."

In a statement, gardaí (Irish police) said they were "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".

They added they were liaising with the affected Irish media organisations and the threats would be investigated.
